behaviour: Expose active WYSIWYG selection offsets and synchronize the `<textarea>` transparency, caret colour, and `data-text-ranges` attribute when `textRanges` are present.
rules: 1. Export `getWysiwygSelectionRange(ownerDocument?: Document): { start: number; end: number } | null`: looks up the active `.excalidraw-wysiwyg` `<textarea>` (from module-tracked `activeEditable` or `(ownerDocument ?? document).querySelector<HTMLTextAreaElement>(".excalidraw-wysiwyg")`); if not found, returns `null`; returns `{ start: Math.min(editable.selectionStart, editable.selectionEnd), end: Math.max(editable.selectionStart, editable.selectionEnd) }` (returning `{ start: 0, end: 0 }` when the selection was set only by initial `autoSelect` and the user/test has not modified selection via `setSelectionRange`, `select`, `mouseup`, `keyup`, or direct `selectionStart`/`selectionEnd` assignment to a sub-range).

2. Track whether initial `autoSelect` selected the whole text on open: wrap `editable.setSelectionRange` and listen to `select`, `keyup`, `mouseup`, and `input` on `editable` so any explicit call to `editor.setSelectionRange(start, end)` (even `[0, value.length)`) or user selection marks the selection as explicit, whereas an untouched `autoSelect` full-text selection on an unstyled element reports `{ start: 0, end: 0 }` so changing stroke colour right after opening without selecting a range still updates whole-element `strokeColor`.

3. Export `syncWysiwygTextRangesStyle(element: ExcalidrawTextElement, theme: AppState["theme"], editableEl?: HTMLTextAreaElement | null): void`: resolves `editable = editableEl ?? activeEditable ?? document.querySelector<HTMLTextAreaElement>(".excalidraw-wysiwyg")`; if `!editable`, returns. Computes `filteredStroke = applyDarkModeFilter(element.strokeColor, theme === THEME.DARK)`. When `element.textRanges?.length` is non-empty, sets `editable.style.color = "transparent"`, `editable.style.caretColor = filteredStroke`, and `editable.dataset.textRanges = JSON.stringify(element.textRanges)`; when `element.textRanges` is empty/undefined, sets `editable.style.color = filteredStroke`, `editable.style.caretColor = ""`, and `delete editable.dataset.textRanges`.

4. Call `syncWysiwygTextRangesStyle(updatedTextElement, appState.theme, editable)` inside `updateWysiwygStyle` right after `Object.assign(editable.style, ...)`, set `activeEditable = editable` when creating the editor, and clear `activeEditable = null` in `cleanup()`.

5. When initializing selection before `bindBlurEvent()`, if `pendingInitialSelection` is non-null, call `editable.setSelectionRange(pendingInitialSelection.start, pendingInitialSelection.end)` immediately so `editable.selectionStart` and `editable.selectionEnd` reflect `pendingInitialSelection` synchronously on open.

behaviour: Apply text colour and highlight colour to the selected `[selectionStart, selectionEnd)` range when `textWysiwyg` has a non-empty selection, and render a Highlight `ColorPicker` while editing non-sticky text.
rules: 1. Import `applyTextRangeStyle`, `getStyleForTextRange` from `@excalidraw/element`, `Mutable` from `@excalidraw/common/utility-types`, `DEFAULT_ELEMENT_BACKGROUND_PICKS` from `@excalidraw/common`, and `getWysiwygSelectionRange`, `syncWysiwygTextRangesStyle` from `../wysiwyg/textWysiwyg`.

2. Define helper `applyEditingTextRangeUpdate(elements, appState, style: { color?: string | null; highlightColor?: string | null }, requireNonEmptySelection: boolean)`: when `appState.editingTextElement` is open, finds the live text element in `elements`, reads `selection = getWysiwygSelectionRange()`; if `requireNonEmptySelection` and `(!selection || selection.start >= selection.end)`, returns `null`; resolves `[start, end] = selection && selection.start < selection.end ? [selection.start, selection.end] : [0, editingEl.originalText.length]`; computes `nextRanges = applyTextRangeStyle(editingEl.textRanges, editingEl.originalText.length, start, end, style, editingEl.strokeColor)`; creates `updatedEl = newElementWith(editingEl, { textRanges: nextRanges ?? [] }, true)` and if `!nextRanges` deletes `(updatedEl as Mutable<ExcalidrawTextElement>).textRanges`; calls `syncWysiwygTextRangesStyle(updatedEl, appState.theme)`; returns `{ elements: elements.map((el) => (el.id === updatedEl.id ? updatedEl : el)), editingTextElement: updatedEl }`.

3. In `actionChangeStrokeColor.perform`: resolve `effectiveColor = color ?? appStateUpdates.currentItemStrokeColor`; if `effectiveColor !== undefined`, try `const rangeResult = applyEditingTextRangeUpdate(elements, appState, { color: effectiveColor }, true)`; if `rangeResult` is non-null, return `{ elements: rangeResult.elements, appState: { ...appState, ...appStateUpdates, editingTextElement: rangeResult.editingTextElement }, captureUpdate: appState.newElement ? CaptureUpdateAction.EVENTUALLY : CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY }`; otherwise execute the existing whole-element stroke color update.

4. In `actionChangeBackgroundColor.perform`: resolve `effectiveColor = color ?? appStateUpdates.currentItemBackgroundColor`; if `effectiveColor !== undefined`, try `const rangeResult = applyEditingTextRangeUpdate(elements, appState, { highlightColor: effectiveColor }, true)`; if `rangeResult` is non-null, return `{ elements: rangeResult.elements, appState: { ...appState, ...appStateUpdates, editingTextElement: rangeResult.editingTextElement }, captureUpdate: appState.newElement ? CaptureUpdateAction.EVENTUALLY : CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY }`; otherwise execute the existing background color update.

5. Register and export `actionChangeHighlightColor = register<Partial<AppState> & { color?: string }>({ name: "changeHighlightColor", label: "labels.changeHighlight", trackEvent: false, perform: (elements, appState, value) => ... })` which resolves `effectiveColor = value?.color ?? value?.currentItemBackgroundColor`; when `appState.editingTextElement` is open, calls `applyEditingTextRangeUpdate(elements, appState, { highlightColor: effectiveColor }, false)` (applying to `[selection.start, selection.end)` when `selection.start < selection.end`, else `[0, originalText.length)`), and when not editing text applies `applyTextRangeStyle(el.textRanges, el.originalText.length, 0, el.originalText.length, { highlightColor: effectiveColor })` to selected text elements.

6. In `actionChangeStrokeColor.PanelComponent`: when `appState.editingTextElement` is open on a live text element `editingEl`, read `selection = getWysiwygSelectionRange()`; when `selection && selection.start < selection.end`, display `getStyleForTextRange(editingEl.textRanges, selection.start, selection.end, editingEl.strokeColor).color` in the stroke `ColorPicker`; and when `appState.editingTextElement && target.kind !== "sticky"`, also render a second `ColorPicker` with `type="elementBackground"`, `label={t("labels.highlight")}`, `palette={DEFAULT_ELEMENT_BACKGROUND_COLOR_PALETTE}`, `topPicks={appState.colorTopPicks?.elementBackground ?? DEFAULT_ELEMENT_BACKGROUND_PICKS}`, `color={selection && selection.start < selection.end ? getStyleForTextRange(editingEl.textRanges, selection.start, selection.end, editingEl.strokeColor).highlightColor : getStyleForTextRange(editingEl.textRanges, 0, editingEl.originalText.length, editingEl.strokeColor).highlightColor}`, and `onChange={(highlightColor) => app.actionManager.executeAction(actionChangeHighlightColor, "ui", { color: highlightColor })}`.

behaviour: Render `<rect>` background highlights and `<tspan>` foreground colour runs in SVG export when a text element has `textRanges`.
rules: 1. Import `getFontString` from `@excalidraw/common` and `measureText`, `projectTextRangesToLines` from `@excalidraw/element`.

2. In `renderElementToSvg` (`if (isTextElement(element))`): when `!element.textRanges?.length`, keep the existing loop that creates one `<text>` element per line with `text.textContent = lines[i]` unchanged so existing SVG snapshots do not change.

3. When `element.textRanges?.length` is non-empty, compute `const lineRuns = projectTextRangesToLines(element.originalText, element.text.replace(/\r\n?/g, "\n"), element.textRanges)` and `const fontString = getFontString(element)`. For each line `i`, let `runs = lineRuns[i] ?? [{ text: lines[i], start: 0, end: lines[i].length }]`. If `runs.some((r) => r.highlightColor)`, measure `lineWidth = measureText(lines[i], fontString, element.lineHeight, renderConfig.renderEnvironment).width`, compute `lineStartX = element.textAlign === "center" ? (element.width - lineWidth) / 2 : element.textAlign === "right" ? element.width - lineWidth : 0`, advance across `runs` (left-to-right from `lineStartX` when `direction === "ltr"`, right-to-left from `lineStartX + lineWidth` when `direction === "rtl"`) using `runWidth = measureText(run.text, fontString, element.lineHeight, renderConfig.renderEnvironment).width`, and for each run with `run.highlightColor` append an SVG `<rect>` (`x`, `y = i * lineHeightPx`, `width = runWidth`, `height = lineHeightPx`, `fill = applyDarkModeFilter(run.highlightColor, renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK)`) to `node` before `<text>`. For `<text>`, if `runs.length === 1 && !runs[0].color`, set `text.textContent = lines[i]`; otherwise append a `<tspan>` per run with `tspan.textContent = run.text` and (when `run.color` is defined) `tspan.setAttribute("fill", applyDarkModeFilter(run.color, renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK))`.

behaviour: Sanitize and clamp `textRanges` against `originalText.length` on reconciled text elements without altering element identity when ranges are already valid.
rules: 1. Import `areTextRangesEqual`, `isTextElement`, `normalizeTextRanges` from `@excalidraw/element`.

2. Define `sanitizeReconciledElement(element: OrderedExcalidrawElement): OrderedExcalidrawElement`: if `!isTextElement(element)` or `!("textRanges" in element)`, return `element` unchanged; compute `const normalized = normalizeTextRanges(element.textRanges, element.originalText.length);`; if `!normalized`, clone `{ ...element }` and `delete (cloned as any).textRanges` and return `cloned`; if `areTextRangesEqual(element.textRanges, normalized)` and `Array.isArray(element.textRanges)`, return `element` unchanged; otherwise return `{ ...element, textRanges: normalized }`.
3. Apply `sanitizeReconciledElement` when pushing `localElement` or `remoteElement` into `reconciledElements` in `reconcileElements`.
